source_text:
Ἕκαστος ἡμῶν, ἀδελφοί, ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι εὐαριστείτω τῷ θεῷ ἐν ἀγαθῇ συνειδήσει ὑπάρχων, μὴ παρεκβαίνων τὸν ὡρισμένον τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ κανόνα, ἐν σεμνότητι.
οὐ πανταχοῦ, ἀδελφοί, προσφέρονται θυσίαι ἐνδελεχισμοῦ ἢ εὐχῶν ἢ περὶ ἁμαρτίας καὶ πλημμελείας, ἀλλ’ ἢ ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ μόνῃ: κἀκεῖ δὲ οὐκ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ προσφέρεται, ἀλλ’ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ναοῦ πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον, μωμοσκοπηθὲν τὸ προσφερόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τῶν προειρημένων λειτουργῶν.
οἱ οὖν παρὰ τὸ καθῆκον τῆς βουλήσεως αὐτοῦ ποιοῦντές τι θάνατον τὸ πρόστιμον ἔχουσιν.
ὁρᾶτε, ἀδελφοί: ὅσῳ πλείονος κατηξιώθημεν γνώσεως, τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὑποκείμεθα κινδύνῳ.
thought_title: Each in one's own order, with a warning about Jerusalem's exclusive sacrifices
orientation: Clement is addressing the Corinthian church directly, applying the previous section's teaching about ordered ministry to each believer and warning that greater knowledge brings greater danger.
pass_a_gloss: Each of us, brothers, in his own order let him give thanks to God, being in a good conscience, not stepping outside the defined rule of his ministry, in reverence. Not everywhere, brothers, are sacrifices of continual offering or of prayers or concerning sin and trespass offered, but only in Jerusalem; and there also not in every place is it offered, but before the temple toward the altar, the thing being offered having been inspected for blemish through the high priest and the previously mentioned ministers. Those therefore who do anything contrary to what is fitting for his will have death as the penalty. You see, brothers: by as much as we have been deemed worthy of greater knowledge, by so much more are we subject to danger.

choices.why: τάγμα means an assigned rank or position in an ordered arrangement; 'order' preserves the military/ordered sense that fits Clement's argument about fixed places

choices.english: let him give thanks to God
choices.why: The verb εὐαριστεῖν means to give thanks or express gratitude; the imperative is third-person singular, a command for each individual
rejected: let him be thankful to God
let him offer thanksgiving to God

choices.why: ὑπάρχων is a participle of being/existing; συνείδησις is conscience; the phrase describes the state in which one gives thanks

choices.term: μὴ παρεκβαίνων τὸν ὡρισμένον τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ κανόνα
choices.english: not stepping outside the defined rule of his ministry
choices.why: παρεκβαίνων means stepping aside from or transgressing; κανόνα is the fixed rule; λειτουργίας is ministry per the glossary
rejected: not transgressing the appointed rule of his service
not deviating from the fixed standard of his office

choices.why: σεμνότης denotes dignity, gravity, or reverence; 'reverence' captures the attitude of proper worship
ἐνδελεχισμός is the technical term for the daily continual burnt offering; the genitive construction is preserved literally

choices.english: the thing being offered having been inspected for blemish
choices.why: μωμοσκοπεῖν means to inspect for blemish or defect; the passive participle is rendered literally to preserve the ritual inspection sense
rejected: the offering having been examined for spots
the thing offered having been scrutinized

choices.why: πρόστιμον means penalty or punishment; the construction is literally 'death as the penalty they have'

choices.term: ὅσῳ πλείονος κατηξιώθημεν γνώσεως, τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὑποκείμεθα κινδύνῳ
choices.english: by as much as we have been deemed worthy of greater knowledge, by so much more are we subject to danger
choices.why: The correlative construction ὅσῳ...τοσούτῳ is rendered literally to preserve the proportional comparison; κατηξιώθημεν is passive of deem worthy
rejected: the more knowledge we have been granted, the more danger we face
to the degree we have been counted worthy of more knowledge, to that degree we are more exposed to danger

bible_refs.note: θυσίαι ἐνδελεχισμοῦ (sacrifices of continual offering) reflects the LXX terminology for the daily burnt offering
The restriction of sacrifice to one place (Jerusalem, before the temple) echoes the Deuteronomic centralization of worship
μωμοσκοπηθέν (inspected for blemish) reflects the requirement that offerings be without defect

pass_b_english: Each of us, brothers and sisters, should give thanks to God in his own order, living with a good conscience and not stepping outside the fixed rule of his ministry, in reverence.

Not everywhere, brothers and sisters, are sacrifices of continual offering or of vows or for sin and trespass offered, but only in Jerusalem. And even there they are not offered in every place, but before the temple at the altar, after the thing being offered has been inspected for blemish by the high priest and the ministers mentioned before.
Those, then, who do anything contrary to what is proper to his will have death as the penalty.
You see, brothers and sisters: by as much as we have been deemed worthy of greater knowledge, by so much more are we subject to danger.

problems.quote: sacrifices of continual offering or of prayers
problems.why: ἐνδελεχισμοῦ is 'continual offering' but εὐχῶν here means 'vows' not 'prayers'.
problems.fix: sacrifices of continual offering or of vows
problems.ruling: εὐχῶν here means 'vows' (sacrifice category paired with sin/trespass), not 'prayers'; mistranslation misleads reader.

problems.quote: what is fitting to his will
problems.why: παρὰ τὸ καθῆκον means 'contrary to what is proper/fitting,' not 'fitting to his will'—sense inverted.
problems.fix: contrary to what is proper to his will
problems.ruling: παρὰ τὸ καθῥηκον means 'contrary to what is fitting'; 'fitting to his will' inverts sense, misleading reader.

edits.old: sacrifices of continual offering or of prayers
edits.new: sacrifices of continual offering or of vows

edits.old: contrary to what is fitting to his will
edits.new: contrary to what is proper to his will

last_rejected.fix: the ministers mentioned before → the ministry mentioned before
last_rejected.ruling: λειτουργῶν is plural noun 'ministers/servants'; λειτουργία is 'ministry'. Different forms, no glossary conflict.

last_rejected.quote: what is proper to his will
last_rejected.why: τὸ καθῆκον = 'what is fitting/proper', not 'proper to'; genitive is objective: 'what is fitting to his will' i.e. what his will requires.
last_rejected.fix: what is fitting to his will
last_rejected.ruling: 'Proper to his will' adequately renders τὸ καθῆκον τῆς βουλήσεως αὐτοῦ; genitive nuance is debatable, not a clear error.
